title: regional-gpu-hedging-strategy-and-allocations-2026-03-25
content:
Weekly infra sync focused on regional GPU hedging and short-term allocation adjustments. This is a working doc — quick notes from the 2026-03-25 capacity sync (40 minutes). Highlights, proposals, and owners below.

Attendees:
- Liam Chen (owner)
- Priya Nair (capacity planning)
- Marco Alvarez (regional ops - EMEA)
- Tara O'Neill (private deployments liaison)
- Omar Haddad (SRE)
- Sid Wu (on call)

Purpose:
- Align on hedging plays for next 21 days across NA/EU/APAC.
- Surface near-term risks (scheduled maintenance, vendor spot shortages).
- Decide on burst-credit allocation and cross-region spill rules.

Executive summary:
- Current fleet utilization (7-day rolling average) by region: NA 72%, EU 78%, APAC 66%.
- Forecast shows a potential 12–18% incremental request spike for mid-April (marketing campaign + two enterprise rollouts).
- EU has the tightest headroom due to two reserved job batches and an upcoming node retirement (Apr 2–6).
- Recommendation: implement a 3-week hedging plan combining (1) soft cap burst credits, (2) targeted pre-warm for high-latency routes, (3) temporary cross-region spill policy with cost floor.

Regional snapshot and short-term numbers (working estimates):
- NA: active GPUs 480 (gpus-equivalent), available buffer ~134 GPUs. Weekly growth trend +3%. Good latency margins.
- EU: active GPUs 310, available buffer ~68 GPUs. Weekly growth trend +6%. Two reserved private jobs scheduled Apr 2–6 consuming ~40 GPUs.
- APAC: active GPUs 220, available buffer ~88 GPUs. Weekly growth trend +4%. Preferred for non-latency sensitive batch workloads.

Risks identified:
1) Vendor spot changes in EU region (notice received from cloud vendor about reduced spot pool between Apr 1–10). Impact: 30–50 GPU shortfall if not hedged. Priority: high. Owner: Priya.
2) Node retirement in EU (hardware EOL) requires four racks to be drained Apr 2–6; migration window may cause transient load on remaining nodes. Owner: Marco.
3) Canary rollout for model-x in NA scheduled Mar 29 — if success there could double traffic to a subset of GPUs. Owner: product (noted).
4) Networking maintenance in APAC region scheduled Apr 4 — could increase request latency and reduce throughput. Owner: network infra ops.

Proposed hedging actions (3-week plan):
A. Soft burst-credit allocation (effective immediately)
  - Allocate 10% of current available buffer as 'burst credits' per region that can be consumed without changing autoscaler profiles.
  - If a region drops below 15% buffer, invoke automatic cross-region spill policy.
  - Owner: Liam.

B. Cross-region spill policy (temporary for next 21 days)
  - Spill order: EU -> NA -> APAC (based on cost and latency).
  - Apply a cost-floor check: only spill if estimated added token-cost < 1.5x baseline.
  - Health gating: require < 10% 95th latency delta on candidate routes for 5 consecutive minutes.
  - Implementation: scheduler PR to add 'spill-safety' flag (see PR linked). Owner: Marco + Sid.

C. Targeted pre-warming schedule for high-sensitivity routes
  - Identify top 5 routes by tail-latency per region (list maintained in Ops dashboard).
  - Pre-warm 20% of affected models during predicted peak windows (use warm pools, not long-running reservations).
  - Pre-warm schedule to be validated with resource simulator before commit. Owner: Tara.

D. Emergency reserved buffer (finance-approved temporary credits)
  - Finance confirmed ability to buy short-term reserved capacity in EU for up to 40 GPUs for 7–14 days. Use only if vendor spot fails and cross-region spill insufficient.
  - Approval workflow: Ops -> Finance -> Exec signoff for >$X/day. Owner: Priya.

Experiments / simulations to run this week:
- Adaptive-burst-credit-simulator: simulate different burst thresholds (5%, 10%, 15%) under a +15% traffic spike. Inputs: current per-model QPS distributions. Owner: Omar. Target complete: 2026-03-28.
- Cross-region-latency-safety run: synthetic traffic from EU -> NA candidates to validate 95th percentile delta under spill. Owner: Sid. Target: 2026-03-27.

Operational checklist for next 7 days:
- Priya to lock vendor communication and ask for detailed spot forecasts by region (due 2026-03-26).
- Marco to produce node-drain plan for EU retirement and list of affected reservations (due 2026-03-26).
- Omar to run the simulator and post results to the thread (due 2026-03-28).
- Tara to draft pre-warm plan and runway schedule for top 5 routes (due 2026-03-27).
- Liam to update scheduler config to create 'burst' pool and add auto-trigger condition (PR by 2026-03-29).

Decision log (meeting):
- Agreed to enable temporary cross-region spill with strict safety gates (unanimous).
- Agreed to reserve finance-backed short-term capacity in EU as a last-resort (exec review required if >7 days).

Open questions / blockers:
- Need confirmation on exact cost delta threshold for cross-region spill from finance (is 1.5x acceptable?) -> Finance input required.
- Will private deployments (customer-managed) accept spill to NA? Tara to confirm consent model and update customer communications.

Notes and context snippets:
- This plan assumes the two enterprise jobs in EU cannot be rescheduled. If product can shift one batch by 48 hours, hedging needs significantly reduce.
- Keep observability tags: hedging:eu2026, hedging:na2026, hedging:apac2026 for tracing.

Attachments / linked artifacts:
- Scheduler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-scheduler/pull/211
- Jira: ENGINFRA-4823 (spot-availability-eu)
- Jira: ENGINFRA-4890 (eu-node-drain)

Next sync: ad-hoc daily standups for next 5 days at 09:30 PT, then weekly sync on 2026-04-01 for review.

Action items (condensed):
- Priya: vendor spot confirmation + finance trigger workflow (due 2026-03-26).
- Marco: node-drain migration plan and reservation list (due 2026-03-26).
- Omar: simulator runs and write-up (due 2026-03-28).
- Tara: pre-warm schedule & customer consent for private spill (due 2026-03-27).
- Liam: scheduler config and PR (due 2026-03-29).

If anything urgent surfaces, escalate in #infra-gpu-capacity and tag leads above.

Notes-to-self: follow up with product regarding the model-x canary and the possibility to stagger rollout if hedging cost is too high.

End of notes.
